text: tests/lint-ui.test.ts: `capture()` memoizes into `captured` only on the success path — the assignment is the last statement of the `try`, after both spawns. If either `Bun.spawnSync` throws (e.g. `node` not on PATH in some future environment), `captured` stays `undefined` and every one of the twelve spawning legs re-runs the whole cycle: mkdir under `client/src/components/ui/`, write three files, spawn ESLint twice, remove them again. That is twelve full write/spawn/delete passes over the client source tree on a red, each one briefly materialising files inside `client/src` — noisy, slow, and more chances to leave residue if a pass is interrupted. Setting a module-level `attempted` flag (or caching a captured *error* alongside the capture, and rethrowing it) would make the failure path as cheap and as tree-neutral as the success path. Nothing to fix for this submission — EXAM EVIDENCE shows `bun test tests/lint-ui.test.ts` exit 0, 29 pass, so this path is never taken on the tree the patch describes.

concern: plan-defect: M3 spells the four component assertions as JSX (`<Button>Add</Button>` etc.), but the Proof's `Test:` path is `tests/state-exams/design-system-installed.test.ts` — a `.ts` file, and Bun will not parse JSX in `.ts` (there `<T>` is a type assertion). The exam must use `React.createElement`, or the driver must land the file as `.tsx`. I resolved this for my own verification by running the legs from a scratch `.tsx` file, which I deleted before committing
the legs themselves all pass. This is a disclosure about the exam's landing path, not a claim that any leg cannot pass.

concern: plan-defect: leg (b)'s two token literals are spelled without the space the shadcn CLI actually writes — see the `amends: clause` row. Recorded here only because a later fixture plan regenerating `client/src/index.css` from the CLI without that normalization would go red on the same leg
the leg passes on this tree.

concern: exam: leg (h) [M8]'s regex `/export type \{([\s\S]*?)\} from '\.\/types'/g` counts 2 on any index.ts where a plain `export {...} from './types';` line follows an earlier `export type {` line — the BASE arrangement of this file, so the leg was red at BASE for that reason as well as for the absent `Locator` (the examiner's note reports only the `toContain('Locator')` red above it, which fails first). I did not touch the exam: I made the count honest by putting both `./types` lines at the head of index.ts, which is a real arrangement of the file and satisfies M8's clause as written. Flagging it because the shape is now load-bearing — reorder index.ts again and the leg reddens without any behaviour changing.

concern: exam: leg (a) [M1]'s `declarationOf` slices a declaration to the first `;` in the whole remaining file text, so it cannot read any multi-member type literal written in the repo's own semicolon style. `types.ts`'s `Locator` therefore uses comma-delimited members (`{role: string, name: string}`) where its neighbours (`MutantEdit`, `View`, `Difference`) use semicolons. Same type, no formatter in the repo objects, but it is a local style inconsistency the exam's reading forced rather than one I chose.
